We demonstrate that the characteristic-to-defining shift does not necessarily depend on discrete change in representation or processes. Instead, the shift could fall out naturally from statistical inference over conceptual hypotheses. Our model finds that the shift occurs even when abstract logical relations are present from the outset of learning as long as characteristic features are informative but imperfect in their ability to capture the underlying concept to be learned-a property of our elicited features. 2

Lucariello (1998), Lucariello, Kyratzis, and Nelson (1992) and Lucariello and Nelson (1985), maintain that the first taxonomic categories that are formed are tied to a specific time-space context (e.g. BEDTIME CLOTHING) and this facilitates their recognition. Thus, these categories, referred to as slot-fillers, constitute an intermediate step between thematic and conventional superordinate taxonomic categories, which are abstract (e.g., CLOTHING in general). The progression from thematic to taxonomic categories, passing through thematic-taxonomic categories (slot-fillers), is held to begin approximately at the age of 2 and culminate at the age of 8.
